lesson.title: H muet vs H aspiré
lesson.subtitle: Why l'hôtel and l'homme elide and link, while le héros refuses elision.

hook.title: Why l'hôtel Elides While le héros Blocks Elision: H muet vs. H aspiré
hook.content: Over 90% of French H-words come from Latin or Greek (l'hôtel, l'hôpital, l'homme, l'histoire, l'heure, l'hiver, j'habite) — their H is H muet ('mute H') and allows elision and liaison. A small group of Germanic/loan H-words (like le héros 'the hero' and le huit 'the eight') have H aspiré, which acts like an invisible wall blocking elision and liaison!

footnotes.title: Why 'the hero' is le héros so he doesn't turn into 'zero'!
footnotes.content: If les héros ('the heroes') made a /z/ liaison like les‿hommes, it would sound like /le.ze.ʁo/ — identical to les zéros ('the zeros')!

pattern.title: Latin H (hôtel, homme, heure, histoire, hiver, habiter) = Elide & Link!
pattern.content: Elide and link across all Latin H muet words, while keeping le whole before le héros and le huit.
pattern.linguist_note: Germanic loanwords retained initial /h/ until the 16th century, blocking elision and liaison even after /h/ was lost phonetically.
pattern.trap_note: Never write *le hôtel or *le homme — Latin H muet always elides to l'hôtel and l'homme!

exercises.prompt: Match each H-word with its elision/liaison behavior:

matching_pairs.german: Elides to l' and links with /z/
Elides to l' and links with /z/

exercises.target_answer: Elides to l' and links with /z/, Elides to l' and links with /z/, Elides to l', je elides to j', Blocks elision and liaison (no /z/!)
exercises.meaning: l'hôtel / les‿hôtels (Latin H muet), l'homme / les‿hommes (Latin H muet), l'heure / l'histoire (Latin H muet), j'habite (Latin H muet), le héros / le huit (H aspiré)
exercises.explanation: Both H's are silent in the mouth; H muet allows elision/liaison while H aspiré blocks it.

exercises.prompt: Why does French say 'les héros' WITHOUT a /z/ liaison (/le e.ʁo/), unlike 'les‿hommes' (/le.z‿ɔm/)?
options: Because a /z/ liaison on 'les héros' would sound identical to 'les zéros' ('the zeros')!
Because the H of héros is pronounced like an English H
exercises.target_answer: Because a /z/ liaison on 'les héros' would sound identical to 'les zéros' ('the zeros')!
exercises.meaning: H aspiré blocks liaison so les héros never sounds like les zéros!
exercises.explanation: H aspiré blocks liaison so les héros never sounds like les zéros!

exercises.prompt: Which sentence correctly applies H muet elision across all three words?
options: Le homme habite à le hôtel depuis une heure
L'homme habite à l'hôtel depuis une heure
L'homme habite à le hôtel depuis l'heure
exercises.target_answer: L'homme habite à l'hôtel depuis une heure
exercises.meaning: Both homme and hôtel have Latin H muet and must elide to l'!
exercises.explanation: Latin H muet always triggers elision: L'homme, à l'hôtel.

exercises.idea: in winter the man lives at the hotel
cues: the man lives at the hotel → l'homme habite à l'hôtel
idea_parts: subject + verb + place → l'homme habite à l'hôtel
exercises.target_answer: En hiver, l'homme habite à l'hôtel
exercises.meaning: In winter, the man lives at the hotel
exercises.explanation: hiver, l'homme, habite, and l'hôtel are all Latin H muet words.

diagnosis.cue: Elide le before homme and hôtel: l'homme, à l'hôtel.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: L'histoire de cet hôtel est très intéressante
exercises.target_answer: L'histoire de cet hôtel est très intéressante
exercises.meaning: The history of this hotel is very interesting
exercises.explanation: histoire takes l' and hôtel takes prevocalic cet!
exercises.affirmation: You handled both l'histoire and cet hôtel cleanly.

summary.outcome: Distinguish Latin H muet (l'hôtel, l'homme, l'heure, l'histoire, l'hiver, j'habite) from elision-blocking H aspiré (le héros, le huit).

use_example.english: He is the hero of the story.

summary.takeaway: Both H's are silent; Latin H muet elides (l'histoire), while H aspiré stands apart (le héros).
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([5121] Le Pain, Le Fromage, Le Vin & L'Eau): see how H muet vs H aspiré leads directly into Le Pain, Le Fromage, Le Vin & L'Eau.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "In winter, the man lives at the hotel" in French:
twist.target_answer: En hiver, l'homme habite à l'hôtel
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "En hiver, l'homme habite à l'hôtel" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of H muet vs H aspiré.

hôtel.shift_rule: Norman doublet: S and H dropped
hôtel.etymology_derivation: Latin hospitalis → hostel AND hôtel — the same word entered English twice: once with its S (hostel, hospital), once without (hôtel).

hôpital.etymology_derivation: Compare hospital and hôtel — the circumflex on ô marks the vanished s!

homme.etymology_derivation: Latin homō 'man' — the root of human, homicide, humus (of the earth). The H is written and never said.

histoire.etymology_derivation: One French word covers both 'history' and 'story'.

heure.etymology_derivation: Latin hōra. Silent H triggers elision: l'heure.

hiver.etymology_derivation: Latin tempus hībernum 'wintry season' — English hibernate.

habiter.context_translation: I've lived here for three years.
habiter.etymology_derivation: habitāre 'to dwell often' — a habitat is where a thing dwells; habits are where you dwell repeatedly. With depuis, it stays present tense.

huit.shift_rule: Latin octō, o breathed into hu-
huit.etymology_derivation: Latin octō — octopus, October. French breathed an h in front: huit.
